scenario: AITA for not helping a woman at walmart | I (male 24) started working at walmart for the summer about a month ago. My job mainly involves working with inventory in the back room and not on the floor with customers, sometimes we get heavy boxes that we need to lift as a part of our regular duties. One of my co-workers is a female (fcw) in her early to mid 30s, physically in good shape and as far as I can tell no physical disabilities. (Fcw) approaches me and asks if I can help her lift a heavy box, I say of course and I walk over to the box with her expecting us to perform a team lift - however we get to the box and as I get to one side of the box expecting her to go to the other she just stands there and watches me. I ask "are you ready?" And she says "yes it just needs to go in that bin" (referencing a metal shelving unit about 4 feet high). I say "ok let's do it" and she responds "it's to heavy for me can you please lift it into the bin?". I respond by saying "I'm more than happy to help anyone if they're having trouble with something, but I'm not going to lift all your heavy boxes for you while you stand there watching me" and (fcw) said "if you're not willing to help me I'll find someone who will" and stormed off. Later on the head guy on our team (not my boss just the guy with most seniority who directs us) walks up to me and said " I just spoke to (fcw), the next time someone asks for help you need to help them, that's part of being a team. I responded by clarifying exactly what happened in case she stretched the truth and finished by saying "we're both paid to do the exact same job and if she cant perform the tasks then she shouldn't have taken the job, I'm not the designated heavy lifter on our team and if you would like to discuss this further we can do it with HR present", and at this point feeling pretty annoyed, it was my turn to storm off. So, was I the asshole in this situation? Because so far it seems like its 2 against 1.

First, I'm a 24-year-old male who's been working at Walmart for about a month. My job is mainly in the back room dealing with inventory, which includes lifting heavy boxes. I asked if she was ready, and she said it just needed to go into a bin that's about 4 feet high. I offered to help, but she said it was too heavy for her and asked me to lift it into the bin alone. I told her I was happy to help if she was having trouble, but I wasn't going to lift all her heavy boxes while she watched. She got upset and stormed off. Later, the head guy on our team talked to me and said that next time someone asks for help, I should help them because that's part of being a team. I explained what happened, making sure he understood the situation, and mentioned that if she couldn't perform the tasks, she shouldn't have taken the job. I also said I wasn't the designated heavy lifter and suggested discussing it with HR if needed. Then I stormed off, feeling annoyed. So, was I the asshole here? It seems like two people are against me, but I feel like I was just trying to stand up for myself and not let someone take advantage of me. Let me think about this. On one hand, teamwork is important, and helping out a co-worker seems like the right thing to do. But on the other hand, I was already doing my job, and she was asking me to do her work for her. She didn't seem to be in any immediate danger or unable to lift the box herself. She was just asking me to do it all alone while she watched. I wonder if there's a middle ground here. Maybe I could have helped her lift the box together, showing teamwork, but also not doing all the work myself. Or perhaps I could have suggested that we both lift it together, emphasizing that we're a team and should work together. Also, the head guy's reaction might have been influenced by the company's policies or the team's dynamics. Maybe he felt it was important to maintain a certain level of cooperation, even if it wasn't entirely fair in that specific instance. I'm also considering the possibility that the co-worker felt uncomfortable or was in a difficult situation, maybe she was struggling more than she let on. However, maybe I could have communicated my feelings more clearly or suggested a collaborative approach instead of refusing outright. That way, I still maintain teamwork but also ensure that the workload is shared fairly. So, was I the asshole? I don't think so. I was just trying to do my job and not let someone else's laziness affect my work. But perhaps I could have handled the communication a bit better to maintain a more positive team dynamic.
